name: slack
description: Read-first Slack CLI + read-only MCP server on your own browser session: search, export, download; send/react/edit/invite/add-emoji TTY-gated, create-channel typed-echo with no bypass
surface: MCP read tools + CLI (search, export, read-only file download); `send`/`react`/`edit`/`invite`/`add-emoji` preview then confirm at /dev/tty or `--yes` after a human approved the preview; `upload-file.mjs` is `--yes`-only; `create-channel` requires typing the channel name back with no `--yes`; no delete/kick/archive verb exists

origin.note: ported into this kit from a company-specific Slack MCP+CLI; the workspace is configuration

install.description: Install Node dependencies locally (puppeteer-core, commander, zod, the MCP SDK) from the committed lockfile
install.why: the CLI and the MCP server import these; nothing is installed globally
install.yes: node_modules/ is created inside tools/slack from package-lock.json; no network call to Slack is made
install.no: skipped; every cli.js and server.js invocation fails on import until you run it

env.name: SLACK_WORKSPACE_URL
env.description: Your workspace URL, e.g. https://yourco.slack.com/ or https://grid-yourco.enterprise.slack.com/ on Enterprise Grid. Every API call and the login go through it. Alternative: workspace_url in ~/.config/slack-cli/config.json (mode 600)

env.name: SLACK_ENTERPRISE_ID
env.description: Pin the id the Edge API (user and channel search) is addressed by: the E… org id on Enterprise Grid, the T… team id otherwise. Normally unnecessary — the id is captured from auth.test at login. Alternative: enterprise_id in the config file

env.name: SLACK_PERMALINK_URL
env.description: Host to build permalinks on when it differs from SLACK_WORKSPACE_URL (Enterprise Grid: the API uses the org host, shared links use the workspace host). Defaults to the workspace URL. Alternative: permalink_url in the config file

env.name: SLACK_CLI_PROFILE
env.description: Override the Chrome profile directory used for the SSO session (default ~/.slack-cli/). A path containing 'slack-cli-test' runs incognito and persists nothing

env.name: CHROME_PATH
env.description: Override the Chrome binary location used for the browser sign-in

env.name: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS
env.description: Path to your company's root CA bundle, only if TLS verification fails behind an intercepting proxy. Never disable verification instead: augment the trust store, do not switch it off

env.name: SLACK_BUSINESS_HOURS
env.description: Off-hours gate window for bulk reads as HH-HH in 24-hour time (default 06-18), Monday-Friday. Alternative: business_hours in the config file

env.name: SLACK_BUSINESS_TZ
env.description: IANA time zone the window is evaluated in (default: this machine's zone), e.g. America/Los_Angeles. Alternative: business_tz in the config file

auth.flow: Your own browser session: Chrome (puppeteer-core, visible) opens the workspace URL, you sign in however your company does (any identity provider, MFA included), the tool waits for app.slack.com, then reads the xoxc token from boot_data and the slack.com cookies and caches both to a 600-mode file. No app, no bot token, no scopes beyond what you already have

caches.refresh: node cli.js login — or run any read; Chrome opens when the cache is missing or Slack rejects the session
caches.revoke: rm ~/.slack-cli-auth.json, then sign out of Slack in the browser (a browser session token; Slack invalidates it on sign-out)
caches.note: written mode 600; tagged with the workspace host, so a cache for a different workspace is ignored rather than sent
dedicated Chrome profile dir holding the SSO session; SLACK_CLI_PROFILE overrides

safeguards: Read-first: server.js registers seven read tools and no write tool; every write is a CLI verb, none reachable from the MCP surface (SENSIBILITIES #1)

send (lib/send.js): the recipient is resolved through users.info and a full preview is printed before anything is asked; confirmOnTty() reads /dev/tty — not stdin — and requires the word "send"; --yes skips that prompt and is meant only for a caller that has shown a human the --dry-run preview and been told yes; with no TTY and no --yes the command exits 2 and prints the ways forward
react (lib/react.js): same preview → confirmReactOnTty() on /dev/tty → --yes tier as send; REACT_AUDIT stderr line on every mutation; --remove is the undo

edit (lib/edit.js): chat.update on your own messages only (the author is checked against auth.test first); the current text is fetched and diffed before any prompt; the pre-edit text is written to data/edit-backups/<channel>-<ts>.json (mode 600, append-only revisions[] chain) before the update; refuses when files, attachments, or non-text blocks would be dropped unless --allow-lossy; confirmEditOnTty() on /dev/tty or --yes; EDIT_AUDIT line on every mutation

invite (lib/invite.js): conversations.invite on an existing channel, one call per person, so partial success is reported and never rolled back; the preview states the channel's privacy (an unreadable conversations.info renders UNKNOWN and is treated as private) and names the history disclosure a private invite carries; every invitee is resolved through users.info and shown with their email; confirmInviteOnTty() on /dev/tty or --yes; already_in_channel counts as success; INVITE_AUDIT line per person

add-emoji (lib/emoji.js): the name is validated and the image's format, dimensions and size (<= 128 KB) are read from its header before any network; emoji.list is checked and a taken name is refused before any prompt; confirmEmojiOnTty() on /dev/tty requires the word "emoji", or --yes after a human approved the --dry-run preview; EMOJI_AUDIT stderr line on every upload; no remove verb exists

upload-file.mjs: resolves the recipient, previews, and refuses to deliver without --yes; there is no TTY prompt, so --yes alone delivers — confirm the file and the recipient with the user before passing it

create-channel (lib/create-channel.js): a channel name can never be reclaimed, so confirmCreateOnTty() reads /dev/tty and requires the operator to type the channel name back; there is no --yes and no bypass; without a TTY the command exits 2 and prints the staged command for a human to run; the name is validated before auth and the collision check is advisory only (Slack's name_taken is the arbiter)

Off-hours bulk gating (lib/safeguards.js enforceOffHours): my-messages, channel, mentions, reactions, threads and year-review are blocked Mon-Fri during SLACK_BUSINESS_HOURS (default 06-18) in SLACK_BUSINESS_TZ (default: this machine's zone) unless --force, which proceeds with a warning (SENSIBILITIES #4). One fail-closed exemption (channelReadExemption): `channel` bounded to one search page (--max-pages 1 or --max-results <= 100) of a private channel the caller is a member of, verified by conversations.info is_private and is_member; a public channel, unknown membership, unreadable info, or any multi-page shape keeps the gate
No delete, kick, archive, rename, or join verb exists; the undo for a membership change is a human in the Slack UI

The session cache ~/.slack-cli-auth.json is written mode 600 and tagged with its workspace host; a cache for a different workspace is ignored, not sent. ~/.config/slack-cli/config.json is refused when group/world readable. No verb prints the token (SENSIBILITIES #6, #11)
Per-process telemetry counters (lib/telemetry.js), a default per-request --delay on paginated pulls, and 429 / Retry-After honored with capped backoff

verbs.name: whoami
verbs.note: prints the configured workspace before any network; the first thing to run

verbs.name: find-channels
verbs.note: Edge API keyword discovery; the fallback where conversations.list is admin-restricted

verbs.name: list-channels
verbs.note: conversations.list; may return enterprise_is_restricted on Enterprise Grid

verbs.name: channel-toc
verbs.note: writes channel-catalog.json + CHANNELS.md locally (gitignored)

verbs.name: download
verbs.note: read-only GET of attachment bytes to a local dir

verbs.name: channel
verbs.note: off-hours gate unless a single page of a private member channel; --force overrides

verbs.name: my-messages
verbs.note: off-hours gate; --force overrides

verbs.name: mentions
verbs.note: off-hours gate; --force overrides

verbs.name: reactions
verbs.note: off-hours gate; --force overrides

verbs.name: threads
verbs.note: off-hours gate; --force overrides

verbs.name: year-review
verbs.note: off-hours gate; --force overrides

verbs.name: login
verbs.note: re-authenticates the operator's own session; mutates only the local cache

verbs.name: send
verbs.note: confirmOnTty() on /dev/tty, or --yes after a human approved the --dry-run preview

verbs.name: react
verbs.note: confirmReactOnTty() on /dev/tty, or --yes after preview; reversible with --remove

verbs.name: edit
verbs.note: confirmEditOnTty() on /dev/tty or --yes; diff + 600-mode backup before replace; refuses lossy updates without --allow-lossy

verbs.name: invite
verbs.note: confirmInviteOnTty() on /dev/tty or --yes after preview; private-history disclosure named; each invitee's email shown

verbs.name: add-emoji
verbs.note: confirmEmojiOnTty() on /dev/tty, or --yes after preview; a taken name is refused before the prompt; the undo is a human removing it in Customize Workspace

verbs.name: upload-file.mjs
verbs.note: --yes only — previews without it, no TTY prompt

verbs.name: create-channel
verbs.note: confirmCreateOnTty(): type the channel name back at /dev/tty; no --yes, no bypass — agents get exit 2 and a staged command

verbs.name: delete message
verbs.note: no chat.delete verb exists; an accidental post is edited down, not removed

verbs.name: kick / archive / rename / join
verbs.note: no verb exists; undo is a human in the Slack UI

verbs.name: list_my_channels
verbs.note: conversations.list; may return enterprise_is_restricted on Enterprise Grid

checks.fix: cd {TOOLBELT}/tools/slack && npm ci   (or: toolbelt setup slack) — the CLI and MCP server need these; the unit tests do not
node {TOOLBELT}/tools/slack/cli.js login — Chrome opens for your company's sign-in

smoke_test.expect: after npm ci: help renders; node test.js passes with no network and no workspace configured (test.js alone needs no node_modules — only cli.js/server.js do)

risk.worst_case: a message posted, edited, a custom emoji added, or a channel created in your company's Slack under the operator's name; a channel name can never be reclaimed, which is why create-channel is typed-echo with no --yes
